item.title: [netdata/netdata] v2.12.2
item.description:
netdata/netdata | 81113 stars| 6690 forks.

| Shell | C | C++ | HTML | JavaScript | Makefile | CMake | Python | POV-Ray SDL | Dockerfile |

The fastest path to AI-powered full stack observability, even for lean teams.

Netdata v2.12.2 is a patch release to address issues discovered since v2.12.1.

This release tightens SNMPv3 authentication in the SNMP traps receiver, stops alert evaluation from keeping obsolete charts alive indefinitely, makes Cloud reliably see disconnected children as offline and receive every alert transition, restores the intended backoff when the Agent reconnects to Cloud, requires Function and dynamic configuration requests to carry strict JSON, keeps external plugins running after a single malformed line of output, keeps Kubernetes state charts and their alerts from disappearing when a similarly named object is deleted, makes long-range queries return data from newer tiers after a gap in older ones, and fixes static 64-bit ARM builds that could crash at startup on Cortex-A53 boards such as the Raspberry Pi 3.

Streaming and Netdata Cloud

  • Fixed a race where a child that disconnected from its Parent could stay live in Netdata Cloud. The node state update was scheduled before the child was marked offline, so under CPU contention the offline state was sometimes never sent (#24285, @stelfrag)
  • A Parent now waits 125% of a disconnected child's expected reboot time, capped at 30 seconds, before reporting it offline to Netdata Cloud. Integer arithmetic had reduced the margin to 100%. A child with no recorded reboot time no longer schedules a zero-delay timer, which can cause high CPU usage with older libuv versions (#24343, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed alert transitions being lost on the way to Netdata Cloud. A message the MQTT layer refused, for example while offline or with a full buffer, was treated as delivered and removed from the queue; it is now retried. The alert snapshot also could announce more chunks than it sent, and is now built from a single consistent query and sent only after a successful rebuild (#24224, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed the reconnect backoff to Netdata Cloud. Once the backoff reached its cap, the clamp was returned in seconds but slept as milliseconds, so a disconnected Agent retried about once per second instead of waiting up to the intended maximum (currently 20 minutes) (#24340, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed the Cloud connection handing out MQTT packet id 1 twice when the packet id counter wrapped around. Two messages in flight with the same id lose their acknowledgement and timeout tracking (#24341, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed the t-rx timestamp in the Agent's HTTP replies to Netdata Cloud, which had been sent as 0 since v2.0.0 instead of the time the request was received (#24252, @stelfrag)

Health

  • Fixed alert evaluation keeping obsolete charts alive. Every evaluation pass refreshed the chart's last-access time, so an obsolete chart with an alert attached was never old enough to be cleaned up. On Kubernetes nodes with pod churn this kept growing the number of k8s.cgroup charts, and the metadata on Parents along with it (#24273, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed several health persistence bugs: a prepared statement leaked on every alert transition on hosts without an ACLK configuration, 64-bit event ids were bound as 32-bit values, and the next alarm event id fell back to 0 instead of the alarm id when there were no detail rows (#24223, @stelfrag)

Database

  • Fixed metadata cleanup passes that could stall. A dimension, chart or label cleanup pass never completed if the first row of its snapshot was deleted before being read, and an interrupted context cleanup dropped the context from its queue, leaving the rest of its dimensions unchecked. Failed chart label stores are now retried, and the WAL size is checked far less often during cleanup (#24227, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed a deadlock when freeing a dictionary whose delete callback destroys a nested dictionary that still has referenced items. Tier backfill could reach it when a chart of a removed host was freed while one of its dimensions was still referenced (#24344, @stelfrag)
  • dbengine: corrupted gorilla-compressed pages whose length is not a multiple of the buffer size are now rejected instead of being read past the end of their allocation (#24310, @ArjunD3456)
  • Fixed completed points of higher tiers staying invisible to queries for a full extra tier period. They were published only when a collection landed exactly on a tier boundary, which slow or offset collectors can miss every time; overdue points are now published on the next collected sample (#24405, @ktsaou)
  • dbengine: gaps of a single second are now cached like longer ones, so repeated queries over them no longer search the journals again, and a cached gap no longer overlaps the first point of the page that follows it (#24370, @ktsaou)

Queries

  • Fixed the dimensions= filter of /api/v1/context and /api/v1/contexts, which ignored every metric whose name equals its id (most of them) and so returned all dimensions, instances and contexts (#24245, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed instance@node_id patterns in the weights API (metric correlations, anomaly rates), which matched nothing (#24245, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed label filters that combine a bare label name with a name=value term, so matching charts are kept while negative name=value terms still take precedence (#24202, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed /api/v1/info reading the analytics strings (build info, release channel, notification methods, exporting connectors) without their lock, so a request that overlapped an analytics refresh could read freed memory (#24342, @stelfrag)
  • Fixed queries returning empty rows for the rest of their time range when an older tier ran out of data well before the planned switch to a newer tier. The query now continues into the newer tier, and SES/DES no longer extend stale values to the end of a query whose tier switch failed (#24406, @ktsaou)

Functions

  • Function and dynamic configuration requests now accept only strict JSON request bodies (RFC 8259). Any other body, such as YAML, form data or plain text, is rejected with HTTP 400. The dashboard, Netdata Cloud and the Agent's own callers already send JSON. A saved dynamic configuration that is not strict JSON fails to re-apply, with a warning in the log. Bodies are checked again where they are passed to plugins and streaming children, so update Parents as well as their children (#24409, @ktsaou)
  • go.d.plugin: the body of a Function request is now treated as data up to its end marker. A line in the body that looked like a plugin command could replace the running Function call, cancel another one, or stop the plugin from reading further requests. Malformed or oversized requests are now skipped as a whole, without their bodies being parsed as commands (#24410, @ilyam8)

Collectors

  • External plugins: a protocol error, such as a single corrupted line of plugin output, permanently disabled the plugin until the Agent restarted. Protocol errors now follow the same policy as error exits: the plugin is restarted after 10 × update_every seconds, and disabled only if it never produced useful output or fails more than 10 consecutive runs (#24051, @ilyam8)
  • SNMP traps: SNMPv3 messages are now rejected and counted as usm_failures when they skip authentication for a user configured to require it, or declare a non-USM security model. Rejected messages are not acknowledged and do not register engine IDs (#24188, @ilyam8)
  • SNMP: community strings and SNMPv3 passphrases are no longer included in the connection details written to debug logs (#24217, @ilyam8)
  • Disk statistics: fixed detection of the discard and flush fields in /proc/diskstats. Kernels before 4.18 got six disk_ext.* charts of zeros, and kernels 4.18 to 5.4 got flushes dimensions stuck at zero. The fields are now detected per disk, and flushes dimensions are added when a disk starts reporting them (#24243, @stelfrag)
  • proc.plugin: reduced overhead on kernels where some /proc files are not seekable, such as Ubuntu 24.04 HWE (6.14). Rewinding such a file no longer resolves its name again on every read, cutting proc.plugin busy time by about 9% (#24212, @stelfrag)
  • Kubernetes state: deleting a node, pod, deployment or cronjob no longer removes the charts of live objects whose names start with the same name, such as pods web-10 to web-19 when web-1 is deleted. Those charts did not come back until the object was recreated or the Agent restarted, and their alerts, such as k8s_state_deployment_condition_available, silently stopped. Scheduling a pod also no longer rewrites the node label on such charts (#24402, @stelfrag)
  • log2journal: JSON input with arrays nested deeper than the parser's maximum depth is now rejected with an error instead of overrunning its key stack (#24290, @ArjunD3456)

Installation and packaging

  • Static builds for 64-bit ARM now enable the linker workarounds for Cortex-A53 errata 835769 and 843419, including for the Rust plugins. Depending on code layout, a static build could die with SIGILL at startup on Cortex-A53 boards such as the Raspberry Pi 3 and ODROID-C2. CI now scans the aarch64 static archive for unfixed instruction sequences, and Rust functions are aligned to 8 bytes so the linker's erratum stubs cannot shift them back onto an affected sequence (#24207, @stelfrag, #24387, @vkalintiris)
  • Windows packages now bundle the msys-2.0.dll from MSYS2's own msys2-runtime 3.6.11 package, pinned by URL and checksum, instead of building a patched 3.6.10 runtime from source. 3.6.11 carries the upstream fixes for the startup crash addressed in v2.12.1, and the source build no longer compiled with MSYS2's current toolchain (#24390, @stelfrag)
  • Updated the vendored IBM MQ client libraries to 9.4.5.1 (#24294, @Ferroin)

Acknowledgments

We would like to thank our dedicated, talented contributors that make up this amazing community. The time and expertise
that you volunteer is essential to our success.

  • @ArjunD3456 for bounding the array nesting depth of the log2journal JSON parser and
    for rejecting corrupted gorilla pages in dbengine.

Support options

As we grow, we stay committed to providing the best support ever seen from an open-source solution. Should you encounter an issue with any of the changes made in this release or any feature in the Netdata Agent, feel free to contact us through one of the following channels:

  • Netdata Learn: Find documentation, guides, and reference material for monitoring and troubleshooting your systems with Netdata.
  • GitHub Issues: Make use of the Netdata repository to report bugs or open a new feature request.
  • GitHub Discussions: Join the conversation around the Netdata development process and be a part of it.
  • Community Forums: Visit the Community Forums and contribute to the collaborative knowledge base.
  • Discord Server: Jump into the Netdata Discord and hang out with like-minded sysadmins, DevOps, SREs, and other troubleshooters. More than 2000 engineers are already using it!

Summary of changes:

    • eMudhra intermediate CA compromise:
      the private keys of several eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised.
      • release: updated the Envoy docker images so they no longer trust the compromised
        eMudhra CAs.
      • mobile: removed the AAA Certificate Services and emSign ECC Root CA - G3 roots
        from the root certificate bundle built into Envoy Mobile. Servers whose certificate
        chains only lead to these roots are no longer trusted by Envoy Mobile when it uses
        its built-in bundle.
      • dns_resolver: updated the webpki-roots and rustls-webpki crates used by the
        built-in Hickory DNS resolver, so DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS upstreams no longer
        trust the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs.

    • contrib/istio: peer metadata conversion takes a peer's app name and version from the
      app and version labels again, falling back to app.kubernetes.io/name and
      app.kubernetes.io/version only when those are absent or empty. This makes peer-reported
      source_app, destination_app, source_version and destination_version match the

Compiler from OCaml to Javascript.

CHANGES:

Features/Changes

OCaml versions

  • Compiler/Runtime: support for OCaml 5.6: use the optimization hints
    recorded in the bytecode, support the bit counting primitives and
    Sys.filepath_exists, Weak.get_copy no longer copies
    (#1721, #2227, #2469, #2488, #2493, #2494)
  • Compiler/Runtime: OxCaml: block index and small-int string-like indexing
    primitives; OxCaml-specific primitives are gated on //If: oxcaml
    (#2342, #2463)
  • Compiler/Runtime: support building with Introcaml (OCaml fork with runtime
    introspection), gated by the introspect flag (#2409)
  • Compiler/Runtime: with Introcaml, support runtime introspection
    (Introspect.Print and friends) in JavaScript: the descriptor of a block
    is stored in its header word above the tag (tag | (desc << 8)), the
    block descriptors of the program are embedded, and Marshal.Reserved_bits
    is honored; can be disabled with --disable introspection (#2433)

Compiler

  • Compiler: require sedlex 3.8.1 (#2503)
  • Compiler: faster compilation (about 25% faster than 6.4.1 on large
    programs): new Int_trie and Int_set data structures,
    sharing-preserving Subst and Js_traverse.map, Js_traverse.free as
    an iterator, circular-buffer worklists, faster JavaScript printer and
    lexer (#2445, #2446, #2447, #2448, #2449, #2452, #2454, #2512)
  • Compiler: keep the name of function expressions that do not refer to
    themselves; the unused-js-vars warning now reports such names (#2449)
  • Compiler: emit large binary string constants as base64 literals, which are
    much smaller than \xNN-escaped literals (-14% on the toplevel example)
    (#2432)
  • Compiler: report JavaScript syntax errors as file:line:col followed by
    the offending line; columns start from 1 (#2464, #2471, #2491)
  • Compiler: the JavaScript parser accepts source phase imports
    (import source x from "m") (#2523)
  • Compiler: drop redundant breaks out of labelled blocks, turning the
    blocks into if/else statements or conditional expressions; the nesting
    this introduces is bounded by --set=break_sink_depth, and the
    merge_node_max parameter is renamed label_depth (#2513)
  • Compiler: simplify the generated JavaScript (!x for negated
    conditions, no empty if branches) (#2500)
  • Compiler: omit the | 0 coercion after an unsigned right shift by a
    constant (#2531)
  • Compiler: inline pending expressions at the end of a try body, avoiding
    temporaries such as try{var c = f(x); return c;} (#2532)
  • Compiler: bind identical literals of a bytecode program to a single
    variable, which shrinks the generated code and speeds up compilation of
    programs with many duplicated constants; identical literals may now be
    physically equal (==) (#2547)
  • Compiler: fold if (c) return a; return b into return c ? a : b
    (#2533)
  • Compiler: test integers against 0 by truthiness (!x rather than
    0 === x) when the result is only used as a condition (#2538)
  • Compiler: simplify !c ? a : b into c ? b : a (#2538)
  • Compiler: compare integers directly rather than comparing the result
    of compare with 0 (#2529)
  • Compiler: faster reading of debug events, used with --pretty and
    --debug-info (#2541, #2548)

Effects

  • Compiler: with --effects={cps,double-translation}, specialize calls to
    known functions before the CPS transformation (#2458)
  • Compiler: with --effects=double-translation, only generate a CPS version
    of the functions that may run below an effect handler (#2441)
  • Compiler/Wasm: with --effects=cps, no longer turn mutually recursive
    functions into CPS, since Wasm has proper tail calls (#2441)
  • Runtime: specialize one- and two-argument partial applications in
    double-translation mode (#2437)

Wasm

  • Compiler/Wasm: intern string constants (program-wide with whole-program
    compilation, per compilation unit otherwise) (#2436)
  • Compiler/Wasm: small code generation improvements (negation, physical
    equality on JavaScript values, bigarray dimensions, result types of
    runtime primitives, masking of i31 values, range checks in the runtime)
    (#2472, #2475, #2529)
  • Compiler/Wasm: add --setenv, matching js_of_ocaml (#2415)
  • Compiler/Wasm: emit a sourcemap mapping at the start of each function, for
    the Chrome profiler (#2417)
  • Compiler/Wasm: the linker supports the wide arithmetic and custom
    descriptor instructions (#2515)
  • Compiler/Wasm: store more long-lived toplevel variables in globals; fix a
    crash when one of them is assigned in a try body (#2516)
  • Runtime/Wasm: faster caml_hash, compare, lexer engines, Str
    searches and output_value sharing detection (with WASI, output_value
    now shares boxed numbers with equal contents); single bound check in
    fixed-width Bytes accesses (#2470, #2505)

Libraries

  • Lib: add WebGL2 bindings; the webgl example uses WebGL2 and a new
    webgl2_particles example demonstrates transform feedback (#1226, #2388)
  • Lib: add Crypto (Web Crypto API) bindings (#2380)
  • Lib: add Notification and Clipboard bindings (#2379)
  • Lib: add Service Worker, MessageChannel/MessagePort and Cache API
    bindings (#2381)
  • Lib: add FontFace (CSS Font Loading API) bindings (#2255)
  • Lib: add the Pointer Capture API to Dom_html.element, and
    getPredictedEvents, altitudeAngle and azimuthAngle to pointerEvent
    (#2403)
  • Lib: consolidate the duplicate messageEvent class types into
    ('target, 'data) Dom_html.messageEvent; the old ones are deprecated
    class type aliases (#2382, #2390, #2555)
  • Lib: add Lwt_js_events.mutation/mutations (MutationObserver) (#250)
  • Lib: Lwt_js_events.load/error/abort accept any element, not only
    images (#2404)
  • Lib (breaking): Typed_array.float32Array_fromArray and
    float64Array_fromArray take a number_t js_array t, as required by
    wasm_of_ocaml (#2416)
  • Lib (breaking): remove js_of_ocaml-lwt.logger, as lwt_log is
    deprecated (#2378)
  • Lib: the native stubs of the JavaScript primitives are weak symbols, so
    that they can be overridden (#2435)
  • Lib: add the js_of_ocaml.devtools library, whose
    Js_of_ocaml_devtools.register_formatters installs a custom formatter in
    globalThis.devtoolsFormatters: when the compiler is built with Introcaml,
    Chrome DevTools then displays OCaml values in OCaml syntax
    (Circle ({x = 0; name = "o"}, 1)), expandable to their fields by name;
    JavaScript values embedded in them are left to the console (#2433)

Toplevel

  • Toplevel: new Wrapped and Async APIs, and protocol, worker and
    worker_lwt_client sublibraries to run the toplevel in a WebWorker
    (#66, #833, #2377)

Bug fixes

Compiler

  • Compiler: fix two reference unboxing bugs (#2426, #2489)
  • Compiler: fix an invariant violation with recursive inlining
    (#2482, #2495)
  • Compiler: fix variable coalescing with ES classes (#2462)
  • Compiler: fix unsound corner cases of the JavaScript simplification
    passes: || fusion of effectful conditions, dropped var declarations
    when folding an if, catch-parameter destructuring defaults (#2393)
  • Compiler: fix the printing of JavaScript code: parentheses around optional
    chains, no ES2021 logical assignments, keep the braces around a single
    block-scoped declaration (#2465, #2502)
  • Compiler: keep static on the same line as the class element it modifies
    (Safari 17 misparsed static class fields) (#2420, #2421)
  • Compiler: fix the JavaScript lexer on out-of-range unicode escapes, on
    CR, U+2028 and U+2029 inside strings and templates, on numeric separators
    in the integer part of a float, and on an HTML close comment --> after a
    multi-line comment (#2503, #2524)

Effects

  • Compiler: with --effects=cps or double-translation, fix mutable local
    variables in try bodies and exception handlers (#2484)
  • Compiler: with --effects=double-translation, fix over-applications of
    functions that do not perform effects (#2455)
  • Compiler/Wasm: with --effects=cps, fix an assertion failure on a try
    whose body modifies a local reference, when compiled without -g (#2519)
  • Wasm: unhandled effects raise Effect.Unhandled (--effects=native) or
    Failure (--effects=disabled) instead of failing with a runtime error;
    handlers installed inside assume_no_perform work; --effects=cps no
    longer runs on a JSPI stack (#2434, #2441)

Wasm

  • Compiler/Wasm: x land y was wrongly assumed to fit in 31 bits when only
    a negative operand did (#2490)
  • Compiler/Wasm: fix specialized Bigarray.Genarray.get/set accesses,
    and check the number of indices (#2427, #2505)
  • Compiler/Wasm: fix several bugs of the Wasm linker (#2504)
  • Compiler/Wasm: fix sourcemaps and toplevels on Windows (#2397, #2418)
  • Wasm: embed cmis when building a toplevel with separate compilation
    (#2227)
  • Wasm: the runtime (zstd, blake2, wasi libc) uses a single linear memory,
    as Safari does not support modules with several memories (#2405)
  • Wasm: resolve .wasm assets relative to the runtime file, so that
    required programs work (#2389)

Runtime

  • Runtime: on Windows, the console device names (CON, CONIN$, CONOUT$)
    can be opened from node; they were resolved against the current directory
    (#2525)
  • Runtime: output_value marshals forced lazy values as their value, and
    caml_hash (Wasm) follows forwarded values, as native code (#2486)
  • Runtime: the functions creating arrays of arbitrary length check
    Sys.max_array_length (#2499)
  • Runtime: fix Str.string_partial_match (OSEC-2026-21) (#2492)
  • Runtime: caml_alloc_dummy_mixed takes two arguments (OxCaml) (#2461)
  • Runtime: fix two nat bugs with 32-bit digits (#2460)
  • Runtime: fix comparison between an immediate and a custom block (#2391)
  • Runtime: preserve leading BOMs when converting strings to JavaScript
    (#2414)
  • Runtime: fix the toplevel relocation of unit names with use-js-string
    disabled (#2429)

Libraries

  • Toplevel: keep /static/cmis on the load path across
    Toploop.initialize_toplevel_env (#833, #2377)
  • Tyxml: keep the first of repeated attributes, as browsers do (#968, #2383)
  • Lib: Form.form_elements and Form.get_form_contents skip
    <input type="button">, as a native form submission does; a named one
    was sent as a field with its value (#2466)

item.title: [hashicorp/consul] v2.1.0
item.description:
hashicorp/consul | 30087 stars| 4632 forks.

| Go | Makefile | Shell | HTML | JavaScript | Gherkin | Dockerfile | HCL | Handlebars | SCSS |

Consul is a distributed, highly available, and data center aware solution to connect and configure applications across dynamic, distributed infrastructure.

2.1.0 (October 21, 2026)

BREAKING CHANGES:

  • agent: (Enterprise only) Agent HTTP API request bodies are now limited to 512 KiB by default, including chunked requests and requests with an unsupported method, and oversized requests return HTTP 413 before the body is read in full. Very large /v1/config writes that previously succeeded can now fail. Raise the limit with the new limits.http_max_request_body_size setting if needed.
  • agent: (Enterprise only) Resource API (/api/...) request bodies are now subject to the same limits.http_max_request_body_size limit (512 KiB by default), and oversized requests return HTTP 413.
  • agent: (Enterprise only) GET /v1/agent/connect/ca/leaf/:service now requires service:write on the requested service for every request, including requests served from the agent's cached leaf certificate. Requests with no token or a token without that permission now receive HTTP 403 instead of the cached certificate. Callers must present a token with service:write for the service.
  • catalog: (Enterprise only) Catalog.Register now requires write permission on the node or service of an existing health check when updating it. Tokens that previously updated checks without that permission now receive a permission denied error.
  • cli: Migrated the consul connect redirect-traffic command from iptables/ip6tables to nftables (nft). The command now uses the sdk/nftables package, which applies all IPv4 and IPv6 rules atomically in a single pass via the nftables inet address family, instead of separate iptables and ip6tables invocations. [GH-23785]
  • cli: Transparent proxy exclusions are now validated before rules are applied: user IDs must be numeric and outbound exclusions must be IP addresses or CIDRs. iptables previously also accepted user names, UID ranges, and host names. [GH-23785]
  • cli: consul connect redirect-traffic does not remove iptables/ip6tables rules created by earlier Consul versions. This only matters when upgrading an existing host or VM in place. Before running the new command on an existing host or VM, remove any Consul-managed iptables rules first (see the transparent proxy upgrade guide for a reference cleanup script). Leaving both rule sets in place can cause double NAT or inconsistent traffic redirection. [GH-23785]
  • docker: The official Consul container images now include nftables instead of iptables. Scripts that run iptables inside the Consul image must be updated. [GH-23785]
  • sdk: Replaced the iptables package with a new nftables package for transparent proxy traffic redirection. Traffic redirection now requires the nft binary and a Linux kernel with stateful NAT support in nftables inet family chains, available upstream starting with Linux kernel version 5.2 (some distributions backport this support onto an earlier nominal kernel version, for example RHEL 8+, kernel 4.18+, and its derivatives). There is no automatic fallback to iptables/ip6tables, so hosts without this kernel support will fail to set up transparent proxy redirection. [GH-23785]
  • feature-gates: Gate API Gateway HTTPRoute upstream-routing composition (PR #23294) behind the experimental feature api-gateway-upstream-routing. When disabled (default), the legacy HTTPRoute-to-router shape is preserved exactly. When enabled by an operator after a full datacenter upgrade, service-router rules are composed with HTTPRoute matches, resolver subset definitions are preserved, and discovery-chain watches use the correct HTTP protocol override. Existing agentless API Gateway proxy states are rebuilt automatically when the effective gate value changes.

SECURITY:

  • Upgrade go version to 1.26.10 to address security vulnerabilities. [GH-24067]
  • deps: upgrade github.com/hashicorp/go-discover to v1.5.0, removing the dependency on the archived github.com/hashicorp/vic module. This also upgrades github.com/vmware/govmomi to v0.55.1 and adds an srv provider for cloud auto-join. [GH-24021]
  • security: (Enterprise only) Remove the github.com/hashicorp/consul root module dependency from the test-integ fault-injection tests to address CVE-2026-15972 and CVE-2026-88021.
  • security: Remove the github.com/hashicorp/consul root module dependency from the envoy integration test SDS server, the consul-container and test-integ test modules, and the proto-gen-rpc-glue e2e fixture to address CVE-2026-15972. [GH-24043]
  • deps: Upgrade github.com/hashicorp/raft-wal to v0.5.0 (with raft v1.8.0, serf v0.11.0, memberlist v0.7.0 and go-metrics v0.7.0), removing the dependency on github.com/coreos/etcd. [GH-23985]
  • deps: Upgrade golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 to address GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6617 and GO-2026-6612. [GH-23994]
  • docker: Run apk upgrade when building the Alpine-based container images so base-image packages (such as sqlite and jq) are up to date. [GH-23964]
  • oauth: (Enterprise only) Avoid an unchecked size addition when merging JWKS key sets during OAuth key rotation.
  • security: Upgrade github.com/klauspost/compress to v1.18.7, go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver to v1.17.10, github.com/moby/go-archive to v0.3.0 and github.com/go-openapi/swag to v0.27.1 to address CVE-2026-63209, CVE-2026-88031, CVE-2026-2303, CVE-2026-17106 and CVE-2026-85280. [GH-23964]
  • ui: Add Content-Security-Policy header to Consul UI HTTP responses to mitigate XSS and data injection attacks. [GH-23971]
  • ui: Pin a newer resolution of morgan to 1.12.1 to address GHSA-9f6g-j8ch-79g4 [GH-23952]
  • Added debounce behavior to enforce a minimum interval between expensive federation-state anti-entropy sync operations. [GH-23196]
  • Update brace-expansion to address GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays). [GH-23786]
  • Update fast-uri to address GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7 (Host Confusion via backslash authority introducer). [GH-23786]
  • Update socket.io-parser to address CVE-2026-69185 (Zero-attachment Memory Exhaustion). [GH-23786]

FEATURES:

  • acl: Add OIDC RP-Initiated IdP logout for tokens created via an oidc auth method: consul logout prints the identity provider's logout URL for the user to open (or opens it in the default browser with the new -open-browser flag or CONSUL_LOGOUT_OPEN_BROWSER environment variable), and the web UI opens it on logout, terminating the IdP session. Activates automatically when the IdP advertises an end_session_endpoint in its OIDC discovery document, or when the logout endpoint is configured explicitly with the new OIDCLogoutURL auth method setting for providers that do not advertise one. [GH-23739]
  • agent: (Enterprise only) Add an inline ai block to service definitions, letting a workload declare its AI role (inference-model, mcp-server, or ai-agent) and role-specific configuration in a single registration via config files and HTTP APIs. [GH-13032]
  • api-gateway: Add http2 and grpc as valid API Gateway listener protocols, enabling end-to-end HTTP/2 and gRPC from client to backend. Previously only http and tcp were accepted; the gateway would silently downgrade gRPC/HTTP2 traffic to HTTP/1.1 on the upstream hop. The new protocols render the correct downstream HTTP connection manager (HTTP/2 codec, h2,http/1.1 ALPN) and align the upstream cluster to HTTP/2, closing the parity gap with Ingress Gateway. [GH-23784]
  • api-gateway: Auto-register DNS for services exposed via an API Gateway, resolvable at <service>.api-gateway.consul. Populates the gateway-services catalog mapping for API Gateways and adds DNS SANs to the API Gateway Connect leaf certificate, bringing API Gateway to parity with Ingress Gateway. The feature is version-gated and backfills pre-existing gateways automatically once all servers are upgraded. [GH-23647]
  • api-gateway: Support zero-touch downstream TLS termination. When TLS { Enabled = true } is set on an api-gateway config entry with no inline/file-system/SDS certificate, the gateway terminates downstream TLS using its Connect CA leaf certificate (with *.api-gateway.consul DNS SANs). Explicitly configured certificates continue to take precedence and are served as SNI overrides alongside the leaf default chain. [GH-23647]
  • api-gateway: add PassiveHealthCheck to gateway-level default upstream limits and route service-level limit overrides, so passive health checking (Envoy outlier detection) can be configured for services routed through an API gateway. [GH-23783]
  • cli: (Enterprise only) consul connect envoy -gateway=inference launches the policy processor alongside Envoy and enforces a minimum Envoy version for the inference gateway. The ext_proc socket is derived per proxy instance; -ext-proc-socket-dir overrides its directory (default /var/run/consul).
  • connect: (Enterprise only) Added an agent-managed OAuth client lifecycle for services with ai.role of ai-agent or mcp-server, including dynamic client registration with IBM Security Verify, key rotation, JWKS publication, and SDS delivery of the OAuth client credential to ai-agent Envoy sidecars.
  • connect: (Enterprise only) Deliver OAuth sidecar credentials as AES-256-GCM envelopes. Content-encryption keys are persisted in KV and served via WorkloadKeyService.FetchKey so consul-obo-outbound can decrypt without becoming an SDS client.
  • connect: (Enterprise only) Wire consul-obo-outbound and consul-obo-inbound ext_proc filters into connect-proxy xDS for hop-bound on-behalf-of token exchange.
  • connect: (Enterprise only) Register services with ai.role of ai-agent or mcp-server with IBM Security Verify using private_key_jwt, persist DCR/JWKS in KV, and deliver the client credential to Envoy as SDS GenericSecret JSON for ai-agent workloads. Cluster IAM is an OIDC ACL auth method with EnableServiceDCR=true (agent oauth.iam HCL is rejected).
  • connect: add ecdh_curves to mesh config entries (MeshDirectionalTLSConfig) and tls_ecdh_curves to agent TLS configuration (TLSProtocolConfig) to support configuring allowed ECDH/KEM curves for sidecar mTLS and agent RPC/HTTPS/gRPC, with automatic hybrid Post-Quantum X25519MLKEM768 curve injection when tls_min_version is set to TLSv1_3. [GH-23884]
  • feature-gates: Add Raft-backed dynamic feature gate framework (Phase 1). A new feature_gates { bootstrap = { ... } } server configuration block seeds the first Raft policy. The leader continuously reconciles desired policy, minimum-version eligibility, and registry defaults into a committed resolved status. Every server runs an atomic cache populated only from committed FSM state; agents consume an indexed resolved snapshot and fail closed until the first generation is delivered. New operator CLI commands consul operator feature list, get, and set provide CAS-safe, ACL-protected inspection and control of feature gates.
  • operator: Add GET /v1/operator/features, GET /v1/operator/feature/:name, and PUT /v1/operator/feature/:name HTTP endpoints for reading and updating feature gate state. Reads require operator:read; writes require operator:write. All reads are blocking-query capable. [GH-23791]
  • inference-gateway: (Enterprise only) Route opted-in external inference models through a terminating gateway. Models marked with the terminating-gateway egress are discovered from the catalog, resolved through the mesh discovery chain, and load-balanced across healthy terminating-gateway replicas, with capability-pool priority tiers and fail-closed behavior when no valid transport is available. A capability pool containing an external model is rejected, and its capability route returns 503, when two of its models render the same endpoint address or its model weights cannot be represented exactly.
  • inference-gateway: (Enterprise only) Add the inference-gateway service kind and config entry. The gateway terminates inbound mesh mTLS, enforces intentions, and applies PII and routing policy through an ext_proc filter to a co-located policy processor. Model upstreams are services registered with ai.role = "inference-model" that intentions allow and that are reachable through the mesh (connect-enabled or behind a terminating gateway). The gateway connects to them over mTLS and selects them by capability, failing over across providers by priority.
  • telemetry: (Enterprise only) Added server-side product usage metrics for ACL auth method counts (OIDC, Kubernetes, JWT) and audit logging config.
  • telemetry: (Enterprise only) Added server-side product usage metrics for mesh gateway mode counts: consul.usage.mesh_gateway_remote.count and consul.usage.mesh_gateway_local.count report the number of service instances configured to use each mesh gateway mode, and consul.usage.mesh_gateway_none.count reports the number of service instances with no explicit mesh gateway mode (unset or none).
  • telemetry: (Enterprise only) Added server-side product usage metrics for service intention default policy, service intention L7 and JWT counts
  • telemetry: (Enterprise only) Added the server-side product usage metric consul.usage.mesh_gateway_enabled, which reports whether any mesh gateway instance is registered in the cluster. It is independent of the mesh gateway mode counts: those count connect-proxy sidecars by their upstream routing mode, while this reports whether the gateway capability is deployed at all.
  • terminating-gateway: (Enterprise only) Add Vault-backed credential injection at the terminating gateway egress. A TerminatingGateway config entry now carries a CredentialInjection block (ext_proc processor UDS path and message timeout) and each linked service can declare a Credential binding (Mode: "inject" with a BindingID). At egress, an ext_proc filter calls a co-located processor that injects the bound credential (e.g. a provider API key sourced from Vault) into the upstream request, so credentials are never stored in mesh config or exposed to clients.
  • xds: Add an inline "virtual DNS" UDP listener (127.0.0.1:8653) that serves an in-memory FQDN-to-VIP table derived from the proxy snapshot. It advertises VIPs for explicit upstreams, intention-allowed upstreams in transparent proxy mode, and cluster peering upstreams, while skipping cross-partition VIPs, stale/unauthorized discovery chains, and empty or non-IP entries so DNS responses stay in sync with what the transparent-proxy listener will actually intercept. Add an optional "egress DNS" UDP listener (127.0.0.1:8654) that forwards queries to agent-configured DNS recursors via c-ares when recursors are present. Extend the xDS ConfigFetcher interface (and agent implementation) to expose DNS recursors. [GH-23698]

IMPROVEMENTS:

  • chore: Update of actions/cache/restore from 4.2.0 to 6.1.0
  • chore: Update of actions/download-artifact from 4.1.7 to 8.0.2 [GH-13634]
  • chore: Update of actions/upload-artifact from 4.3.3 to 7.0.2 [GH-13635]
  • chore: Update of hashicorp/vault-action from 3 to 4 [GH-13636]
  • connect: (Enterprise Only) update compatibility tests to Nomad ENT v1.9.13+ent, v1.10.17+ent, v1.11.11+ent, v2.0.7+ent and Vault ENT 1.19.22+ent, 1.20.16+ent, 1.21.11+ent, 2.0.4+ent, 2.1.1+ent and envoy 1.39.4, 1.38.7, 1.37.9, 1.36.13
  • connect: revert the maximum supported Envoy version from 1.39.4 back to 1.39.1. Envoy 1.39.4 support, listed in a prior release note, is not included in this release. [GH-24057]
  • connect: deliver the sidecar proxy's leaf certificate and CA roots to Envoy over SDS instead of embedding them inline in the public listener. Leaf certificate rotation is now a hitless hot-swap that no longer changes the listener filter chain hash, so established connections (notably long-lived TCP sessions) are no longer drained and terminated on every rotation. [GH-23938]
  • terminating-gateway: deliver each linked service's Connect leaf certificate and the shared CA roots to Envoy over SDS instead of embedding them inline in the gateway's downstream filter chains. Leaf rotation no longer changes the filter chain hash, so established connections through the gateway are no longer drained. [GH-23938]
  • api-gateway: add invert field to HTTPHeaderMatch in http-route config entries, enabling negated header match conditions (e.g. "route when header is absent" or "route when header value does NOT match"). Brings API Gateway to parity with the Ingress Gateway's existing Invert support in service-router. [GH-23817]
  • ci: (Enterprise only) Increased the stale PR automation windows to 90 days before marking a pull request stale and 60 days before closing it. [GH-13119]
  • peering: (Enterprise only) Add support for routing traffic to named ports on peered multiport services. [GH-13142]
  • telemetry: (Enterprise only) Added three product usage metrics for auto-encrypt visibility. consul.usage.client_agent_metric_included reports whether client-agent metrics collection is enabled. consul.usage.client_auto_encrypt_enabled.count and consul.usage.server_auto_encrypt_enabled.count reports the number of clients and servers, respectively, with auto_encrypt.tls enabled. consul.usage.auto_encrypt_enabled combines both counts into a single boolean — true if auto-encrypt is enabled anywhere in the cluster be it client or server.
  • telemetry: (Enterprise only) Added three server-side product usage metrics, consul.usage.api_gateway.enabled reports whether any API gateway instances are currently registered in the cluster, consul.usage.mesh.service.percentage reports the percentage of service instances that are connect-proxy sidecars and consul.usage.transparent_proxy.enabled.percentage reports the percentage of connect-proxy instances that have transparent proxy mode enabled.
  • ui: Migrate the Consul UI to the HashiCorp Design System (HDS). This covers the global navigation shell and breadcrumbs, the list pages (key/value, peers, auth methods, services, service instances, nodes, intentions, linked services, upstreams, and access control), and the access control, namespace, and admin partition forms. Includes numerous accessibility (A11y) fixes. [GH-23911]
  • xds: (Enterprise only) External inference-model upstreams are rendered with a destination-specific mTLS transport socket (per-model SDS validation context and SNI/SAN matching), so the gateway-to-model hop for terminating-gateway-fronted models is mutually authenticated and encrypted per model.
  • xds: (Enterprise only) The builtin/ext-proc Envoy extension now supports Unix domain socket processor targets via Target.Path.

BUG FIXES:

  • gateway: Fix a data race in the API gateway controller where the route reconciler kept adding to a WatchSet after handing it to a controller trigger that was already iterating it. The trigger is now registered only after all discovery chain reads are complete. [GH-24018]
  • ui: Render tab content inside its tab panel so assistive technology can associate it with its tab, and keep focus on a tab after activating it [GH-24013]
  • ui: Show errors loading a tab's content inside the page instead of as a second nested page [GH-24013]
  • acl: (Enterprise only) Fixed Envoy escape-hatch key matching in Proxy.Config and per-upstream config so it follows the same case-folding rules as the config decoders. Keys that differ only by Unicode case folding (for example envoy_local_cluſter_json), and Go field-name forms such as EnvoyListenerJSON, now require mesh:write like their canonical spellings.
  • agent: (Enterprise only) Fixed audit logging so request-body capture respects the body-size limit, uses the decoded request path when excluding KV bodies (for example /v1/k%76/...), and skips /v1/txn bodies. POST /v1/operator/audit-hash now returns HTTP 413 for oversized bodies.

  • proxycfg: Fixed a goroutine and memory leak where transparent proxies registered a new health watch for every imported peered service each time the imported services list changed, and never stopped watches for removed upstreams. [GH-23990]

Trailing semicolon-separated fields in the client certificate component of the x-forwarded-client-cert (XFCC) header (such as auto-registered DNS SANs) are now properly accepted by the RBAC principal regular expression. [GH-23920]

Per-source metadata (-meta) continues to use the deprecated legacy intention API and is only supported in the default partition; combining -meta with a non-default partition now fails with a clear, actionable error. To attach metadata to intentions in an admin partition, use a service-intentions config entry with entry-level Meta via consul config write.
  • connect: (Enterprise only) Attach outbound OBO only for identity-plane upstreams (ai-agent / mcp-server). Explicit HTTP upstreams to inference-gateway or inference-model destinations no longer get consul-obo-outbound and fail closed with "OBO audience not configured".
  • connect: Fixed a bug where Consul servers ignored the configured default_intention_policy for three server-side surfaces — the intention check API (consul intention check, GET /v1/connect/intentions/check), the service topology view (Internal.ServiceTopology), and transparent proxy upstream discovery (Internal.IntentionUpstreams) — and fell back to acl.default_policy instead. This only changes behavior when default_intention_policy and acl.default_policy are set to opposite values; when they agree (or default_intention_policy is unset) there is no change. item.title: [ponylang/ponyc] 0.77.1
item.description:
ponylang/ponyc | 6205 stars| 440 forks.

| C++ | C | GAP | Shell | Pony | CMake | Dockerfile | PowerShell | Python |

Pony is an open-source, actor-model, capabilities-secure, high performance programming language

Add GNU Info backend to pony-doc

pony-doc can now generate GNU Info documentation with --backend info. The output is a single .info file readable by any Info viewer — Emacs, standalone info, or pinfo.

pony-doc --backend info ./my-package

The default backend remains mkdocs, so existing invocations are unchanged.

Fix Base64.encode_url emitting NUL bytes instead of stripping padding

Base64.encode_url with the default pad = false wrote NUL bytes where padding characters would go, instead of omitting them. The NUL-padded output was then rejected by Base64.decode_url as invalid base64.

Base64.encode_url now strips padding entirely when pad = false.

Fix String.find and contains matching past the end of the string

String.find, contains, and rfind compared the needle byte by byte without checking that it fit within the string at each candidate position. When the needle extended past the string's size, the comparison read the null terminator or, for a trim view sharing a larger buffer, bytes from the parent string. count and split_by inherited the problem through find.

let s: String val = "abcd".trim(0, 2) // "ab", backed by "abcd"
s.contains("bc") // was true, now false
s.find("bc")?     // was 1, now raises error
s.count("bc")     // was 1, now 0

Fix Format.float with FormatFix truncating output longer than 30 characters

Format.float used a fixed 31-byte buffer for the formatted output. Values that need more than 30 characters in FormatFix notation — any float whose integer part exceeds 30 digits, such as 1e300 — were silently truncated.

// was: "100000000000000005250476025520" (30 chars, truncated)
// now: the full 301-digit representation
Format.float[F64](1e300 where fmt = FormatFix, prec = 0)

Fix Sort stack overflow on degenerate inputs

Sorting an already-sorted, reverse-sorted, or all-equal array of moderate size (around 100,000 elements or more, depending on the platform's stack limit) caused a stack overflow. Sorting these inputs now completes in O(n log n) time regardless of input pattern.

Fix Base64.decode returning extra bytes for unpadded input with non-zero trailing bits

When unpadded Base64 input does not divide evenly into bytes, the leftover bits at the end are padding and must be discarded. Base64.decode and decode_url instead emitted those trailing bits as an extra byte when they were non-zero. A single Base64 character (6 bits) incorrectly decoded to one byte, and two characters (12 bits) produced two bytes instead of one.

// Before:
Base64.decode[Array[U8] iso]("Q")?   // [64] — wrong, 6 bits can't fill a byte
Base64.decode[Array[U8] iso]("QR")?  // [65; 16] — wrong, trailing 4 bits emitted

// After:
Base64.decode[Array[U8] iso]("Q")?   // [] — 6 bits, no complete byte
Base64.decode[Array[U8] iso]("QR")?  // [65] — 12 bits, one byte plus discarded padding

Fix JSONParser.parse accepting trailing incomplete tokens

JSONParser.parse accepted input containing a valid JSON value followed by an incomplete token — for example, "nulln" or 1 "x. Instead of reporting an error, it silently ignored the trailing content and returned the first value. It now returns a parse error for any input where content remains after the first value.

Fix Format.int with FormatUTF32 printing decimal digits for U8, U16, I8, and I16

Format.int with FormatUTF32 produced the decimal representation instead of the UTF-32 character for U8, U16, I8, and I16 values.

// was: "65"
// now: "A"
Format.int[U8](65, FormatUTF32)

Fix Format.int producing invalid UTF-8 with multi-byte fill characters

Format.int with a fill character outside the ASCII range produced invalid UTF-8. The formatter builds the digit string in reverse, then reverses it byte by byte — multi-byte fill characters had their UTF-8 bytes reversed along with the digits.

// U+00E9 is C3 A9 in UTF-8
Format.int[U8](0 where width = 2, fill = 0xE9)
// was: A9 C3 30 (invalid UTF-8)
// now: C3 A9 30 (valid UTF-8: "é0")

Format on strings with the same fill was unaffected.

Fix Format.apply not applying prec for strings

Format.apply did not apply the prec parameter. Format("hello" where prec = 2) returned "hello" instead of "he". When width was also set, output was wider than width — Format("hello" where prec = 2, width = 4, align = AlignRight) returned " hello" (7 characters) instead of " he" (4 characters).

Fix NormalizeURI not lowercasing characters decoded from percent-encoding in the host

NormalizeURI left decoded uppercase letters in the host un-lowered. NormalizeURI on http://%41B.example/ produced http://Ab.example/ instead of http://ab.example/, and normalizing the result again changed it, breaking idempotency. URIEquivalent reported http://%41B.example/ and http://ab.example/ as not equivalent.

Fix IRegexpCompiler.parse rejecting literal ^

IRegexpCompiler.parse rejected patterns containing a bare ^, reporting a parse error at the caret's position. RFC 9485's NormalChar range includes ^ (0x5E) — I-Regexp has no anchors, so ^ is an ordinary literal outside [...].

match IRegexpCompiler.parse("^")
| let re: IRegexp => re.is_match("^") // now: true
| let e: IRegexpParseError => e.string()
  // was: "I-Regexp error at offset 0: Invalid character encoding"
end

The escaped form \^ (written "\\^" in a Pony string) was already accepted. Patterns like "a^b" now compile and match the literal string "a^b".

Fix IsPrime returning wrong results for primes near the type maximum

IsPrime reported primes near the maximum of an unsigned integer type as composite. For U64, primes near U64.max_value() caused the function to run indefinitely instead of returning.

IsPrime[U32](4294967291) // was false, now true (4294967291 is the largest U32 prime)
IsPrime[U16](65521)      // was false, now true (65521 is the largest U16 prime)

Fix List.rvalues() and List.rnodes() yielding only the first element

Both methods returned only the first element of the list instead of iterating in reverse; they now yield every element from last to first.

let l = List[String].from(["a"; "b"; "c"])
for v in l.rvalues() do
  env.out.print(v)
end
// was:  a
// now:  c, b, a

Fix signed mod producing wrong results when divisor is min_value

mod and %% on signed integers returned wrong results when the divisor was min_value() and the dividend was positive. The result depended on the optimization level — debug builds produced the correct value, release builds did not. modc had the same problem.

I32(1).mod(I32.min_value()) // was: wrong in release builds
                             // now: -2147483647

Fix URITemplate.expand not percent-encoding non-ASCII literal characters

URITemplate.expand copied literal text from the template verbatim, so a template containing non-ASCII characters produced a result with raw UTF-8 bytes instead of a valid URI. Variable values in the same template were correctly percent-encoded.

// template with non-ASCII literal text
match URITemplateParse("café")
| let t: URITemplate =>
  t.expand(URITemplateVariables)
  // was: "café" (raw bytes C3 A9)
  // now: "caf%C3%A9"
end

Fix HashMap.insert_if_absent returning wrong value when insertion triggers resize

insert_if_absent returned the wrong value when inserting a new key caused the map to grow. The value was stored correctly — only the return value was wrong.

Fix _FormatInt allocation hint overflow when prec defaults to -1

_FormatInt.u8, u16, u32, and u64 computed their initial String allocation as (prec + 1).max(width.max(31)). When prec was the default -1 (USize.max_value()), prec + 1 wrapped to 0, producing an allocation hint of width.max(31) regardless of the requested precision. The u128 variant already used the resolved prec' and was unaffected.

All four methods now use prec' (the sentinel-resolved value) in their allocation hint, matching u128.

Fix Iter.dedup() and Iter.unique() returning has_next() = true when exhausted

Iter.dedup() and Iter.unique() reported has_next() = true when the remaining source elements were all duplicates. next() would then error, violating the Iterator contract. This caused last(), nth(), and find() to error on valid input when trailing elements were duplicates.

// was: error
// now: 0
Iter[U64]([as U64: 0; 0].values()).dedup[HashEq[U64]]().last()?

// was: error
// now: 2
Iter[U64]([as U64: 1; 2; 1].values()).unique[HashEq[U64]]().last()?

Fix help for nested CLI subcommands

The help subcommand and --help flag in the cli package could only show help for top-level commands. Requesting help for a nested command path — app help config server or app config server --help — failed with "too many positional arguments" or "unknown command" instead of printing the subcommand's help text.

Both paths now accept multi-level command paths and display the correct help.

Fix Iter.take_while() returning rejected elements after has_next() returns false

Iter.take_while() had a bug where has_next() returned false on the first call after the predicate rejected an element, but true on the second call, and next() then yielded the rejected element. This broke nth() and any code that called has_next() more than once after the predicate failed.

// was: has_next() false, then true; next() returned 5
// now: has_next() stays false
let tw = Iter[U64]([as U64: 5; 1].values())
  .take_while({(x) => x < 3 })
tw.has_next() // false
tw.has_next() // false (was true)

// was: returned 5 (a rejected element)
// now: error
Iter[U64]([as U64: 5; 1].values())
  .take_while({(x) => x < 3 })
  .nth(1)?

Fix Format.float ignoring align and fill parameters

Format.float accepted align and fill parameters but ignored them — output was always right-aligned with spaces regardless of the values passed. Format.int with the same arguments worked correctly.

Format.float[F64](1.5 where width = 8, align = AlignLeft, fill = '*',
  prec = 2, fmt = FormatFix)
// was: "    1.50"
// now: "1.50****"

Fix float-to-integer saturation at the representability boundary

Safe float-to-integer conversions saturate out-of-range values to the target type's min or max. When the integer max was not exactly representable in the source float type, the float representation rounded up to the next power of two, and a float value at that exact boundary was not caught by the saturation check. The value fell through to the raw conversion, which is undefined behavior in LLVM and produced the target type's min on x86-64.

F32(2147483648).i32() returned I32.min_value() instead of I32.max_value(). The same problem affected F64(9223372036854775808).i64(), F32(170141183460469231731687303715884105728).i128(), F32(4294967296).u32(), and F64(18446744073709551616).u64().

All float-to-integer conversions now saturate correctly at the boundary.

Fix JSONPathParser rejecting whitespace between segments

JSONPathParser rejected valid JSONPath queries that had whitespace between segments, such as $ .a, $.a .b, and $.a ['b']. RFC 9535 section 2.1.1 allows optional whitespace before each segment. These queries now parse and evaluate correctly.

Fix GreatestCommonDivisor returning negative values for signed inputs

GreatestCommonDivisor returned a negative value when the second argument was negative. The greatest common divisor is positive by definition.

GreatestCommonDivisor[I64](4, -6)?  // was: -2, now: 2
GreatestCommonDivisor[I64](-4, -6)? // was: -2, now: 2
GreatestCommonDivisor[I8](1, -1)?   // was: -1, now: 1

When both arguments are min_value() of a signed type, the positive result cannot be represented and the call now errors. Previously it silently returned the negative min_value().

Fix JSONPathParser accepting integers RFC 9535 does not allow

JSONPathParser accepted queries with negative zero ($[-0]), leading zeros ($[01]), and a lone minus sign ($[-:]) in index and slice positions. RFC 9535 section 2.3.3.1 defines int = "0" / (["-"] DIGIT1 *DIGIT), so these are not well-formed and must be rejected. These queries now return JSONPathParseError.

Fix URITemplate prefix modifier splitting pct-encoded triplets under reserved expansion

URITemplate.expand with a prefix modifier (:N) under reserved (+) or fragment (#) expansion split pct-encoded triplets in the variable value. RFC 6570 counts a %XX triplet as one character for prefix length; the expansion counted each byte separately, cut after the %, and re-encoded the lone %.

let vars = URITemplateVariables
vars.set("y", "%41b")
match URITemplateParse("{+y:1}")
| let t: URITemplate =>
  t.expand(vars)
  // was: "%25"
  // now: "%41"
end

Fix Base64.encode_pem and Base64.encode_mime producing trailing empty lines

Base64.encode_pem and Base64.encode_mime appended an extra CRLF when the input was empty or when its encoding filled the last line exactly (multiples of 48 bytes for PEM, 57 for MIME). Empty input produced "\r\n" instead of "", and exact-line inputs ended with "\r\n\r\n" instead of "\r\n".

Fix Iter.maybe, dedup, and take_while dropping None elements

Iter.maybe, Iter.dedup, and Iter.take_while silently dropped None elements when the element type was None or a union containing None, such as (String | None).

All three methods now handle None elements correctly. One behavior change: Iter[(T | None)].maybe(None) now produces a one-element iterator containing None rather than an empty iterator.

Fix String.utf32 decoding UTF-8-encoded surrogates instead of rejecting them

String.utf32 decoded the byte sequences for surrogate code points U+D800 through U+DFFF as valid characters. RFC 3629 forbids these sequences in UTF-8, and the utf32 docstring promises (0xFFFD, 1) for invalid encodings. runes inherited the problem through utf32.

let s = recover val String.from_array([0xED; 0xA0; 0x80]) end
s.utf32(0)? // was: (0xD800, 3), now: (0xFFFD, 1)

Fix CommandParser rejecting negative number positional arguments

CommandParser rejected negative numbers as positional arguments, reporting them as unknown short options. app -5 with an ArgSpec.i64 positional returned SyntaxError: unknown short option at: '5' instead of parsing -5 as the argument value. The same problem affected ArgSpec.f64 with values like -1.5.

Negative numbers as positional arguments now parse directly. The -- separator and named-option forms (-n -5, --num=-5) continue to work.

let spec = CommandSpec.leaf("app", "", Array[OptionSpec](), [
  ArgSpec.i64("n", "")
])?
let cmd = CommandParser(spec).parse(["app"; "-5"]) as Command
cmd.arg("n").i64() // was: SyntaxError, now: -5

Fix JSONPathParser accepting invalid string literals

JSONPathParser.parse accepted JSONPath queries containing raw control characters (U+0000 through U+001F) in string literals, and accepted \' escapes in double-quoted strings and \" escapes in single-quoted strings. RFC 9535 section 2.3.1.1 requires raw control characters to be escaped and restricts each quote escape to its own quote type. These queries now return JSONPathParseError.

// These were accepted, now rejected:
JSONPathParser.parse("$['a\x01b']")  // raw control character
JSONPathParser.parse("$[\"\\'\"]")   // \' in a double-quoted string
JSONPathParser.parse("$['\\\"']")    // \" in a single-quoted string

// Escaped control characters remain valid:
JSONPathParser.parse("$['a\\u0001b']") // \u0001 is the escaped form

Fix Iter.cycle() reporting has_next() = true on an empty source iterator

Iter.cycle() on an empty iterator reported has_next() = true indefinitely while every call to next() raised an error. Code following the has_next() protocol — including for loops and other Iter adapters like chain — either looped forever or, in the case of chain, silently dropped every iterator after the empty cycle in the pipeline.

cycle() now returns false from has_next() when the source is empty.

Fix ParseURI accepting hosts containing ':'

ParseURI and ParseURIAuthority accepted non-bracketed hosts containing :, which RFC 3986 forbids in reg-name.

The parsed URI's string() dropped the empty port, producing output that ParseURI then rejected — parse(uri.string()) failed for a URI that ParseURI itself returned.

ParseURI("http://a:b:/")
// was: parsed with host "a:b"; string() "http://a:b/" rejected on reparse
// now: rejected with InvalidHost

Fix CommandParser accepting malformed short option tokens

CommandParser accepted tokens like -=x and -= without returning a SyntaxError. The cli package grammar requires at least one letter after - for a short option (-a, -abc), but tokens starting with - followed by a non-letter, non-digit character were silently treated as positional arguments. These tokens now produce a SyntaxError.

// Before: no error returned
CommandParser(spec).parse(["app"; "-=x"])  // -> Command

// After: returns an error
CommandParser(spec).parse(["app"; "-=x"])  // -> SyntaxError

Fix PosixDate.format raising on valid formats whose output is 8192 bytes or longer

PosixDate.format raised an error on any valid format string that produced 8192 bytes or more of output. Formats producing shorter output were unaffected.

PosixDate(0).format("a" * 8192)?  // was: error raised
                                    // now: 8192-byte string of "a"s
PosixDate(0).format("%Y" * 2048)? // was: error raised
                                    // now: "1970" repeated 2048 times

Fix URITemplateParse accepting prefix lengths with leading zeros

URITemplateParse accepted templates like {a:01} and {a:0009} as valid prefix modifiers. RFC 6570 section 2.4.1 defines max-length = %x31-39 0*3DIGIT — the first digit must be 1–9, so a leading zero is invalid syntax. These templates now produce a URITemplateParseError.

// Before: accepted as prefix length 1
URITemplateParse("{a:01}")  // -> URITemplate

// After: returns an error
URITemplateParse("{a:01}")  // -> URITemplateParseError

Fix ParseURI accepting malformed IPv6 literals

ParseURI and ParseURIAuthority accepted any bracketed host made only of hex digits, : and ., without validating the RFC 3986 IPv6address grammar. Malformed literals like [::1::2], [1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8:9], and [1.2.3.4] were silently accepted.

ParseURI("http://[::1::2]/")
// was: parsed with host "[::1::2]"
// now: rejected with InvalidHost

Fix IRegexpCompiler.parse crashing on deeply nested group patterns

Parsing an I-Regexp pattern with deeply nested groups — such as thousands of ( followed by a character and matching ) — crashed with a stack overflow. The parser now handles arbitrary nesting depth without crashing.

Fix JSONPath stack overflow on deeply nested queries

JSONPath queries with deeply nested expressions — thousands of nested parentheses, filter selectors, boolean operators, negations, or length() calls — crashed with a stack overflow. Common nesting patterns now parse and evaluate at arbitrary depth. Remaining nesting patterns that the parser handles recursively are rejected with a JSONPathParseError when nesting exceeds 1024 levels.

item.title: [questdb/questdb] 10.1.0
item.description:
questdb/questdb | 17466 stars| 1680 forks.

| Java | HTML | CMake | C | JavaScript | Shell | C++ | Rust | Assembly | Dockerfile |

QuestDB is a high performance, open-source, time-series database

QuestDB 10.1.0

QuestDB 10.1.0 adds new SQL features, makes several query shapes faster, and fixes a large batch of correctness and reliability bugs. New SQL includes SUBSAMPLE for server-side downsampling, the percentile_disc / percentile_cont functions, right-hand filters in HORIZON JOIN, and audited views. Parallel GROUP BY now runs over hash joins, and LATEST ON, symbol LIKE/regex filters, SAMPLE BY ... TIME ZONE and out-of-order ingestion on XFS are faster.

This release contains several breaking changes. Read the Breaking changes section before you upgrade, especially if you use HORIZON JOIN, dateadd() timestamps, INT arithmetic, interval strings such as '1min', or Intel macOS.

For any questions or feedback, please join us on Slack or on Discourse.

See also our prettier release notes page.

Breaking changes 💥

  • HORIZON JOIN without aggregates no longer de-duplicates its output. Add SELECT DISTINCT or an explicit GROUP BY to get the old result. Materialized views over such queries need REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW <name> FULL. #7682
  • HORIZON JOIN rejects unsupported ON predicates with an error. Before this change, it ignored them. #7688
  • INT arithmetic wraps at 32 bits in every context, including under a 64-bit cast or on insert into a LONG column. To compute at 64 bits, widen an operand: secs * 1_000_000L or i::long * j. This reverts #4824 and #7021. #7320
  • Malformed intervals are rejected. SAMPLE BY, timestamp_floor() and materialized view REFRESH intervals must use a one-letter unit (1m, 100T, 1d). Before this change, '1min' was silently read as 1 nanosecond and '100ms' as 1 second. #7702
  • dateadd() projections keep a designated timestamp only for fixed-duration units over the designated timestamp itself. Time-series joins, SAMPLE BY and partitioned CTAS over other dateadd() projections, such as month or year units, now fail to compile. Views that depend on them become invalid. Queries also no longer return an extra hidden ORDER BY column. #7681
  • subsample is a reserved word. Quote existing identifiers with that name, e.g. "subsample". #7013
  • Statements that would suspend a WAL table are rejected at compile time: UPDATE on tables with Parquet partitions, ADD INDEX with cold partitions, and ALTER COLUMN TYPE with read-only partitions. #7666
  • Some partitioned CTAS over a multi-key LATEST ON with a covering index no longer infer the designated timestamp. Specify TIMESTAMP(col) explicitly. #7615
  • Object visibility. In Enterprise, users no longer see tables and views they hold no permission on. In open source, a materialized or live view can no longer reach catalogue functions or SHOW statements through a regular view. #7687
  • HTTP sessions end with their credentials. A request whose Authorization header is rejected gets 401 and closes the session instead of falling back to the session cookie. #7799
  • Bundled Java client: sf_max_total_bytes now caps a sender pool as a whole rather than each sender. #7736
  • x86-64 (Intel) macOS is no longer supported. QuestDB no longer ships native binaries for that platform. #7555

Highlights

SUBSAMPLE: server-side downsampling

The new SUBSAMPLE clause cuts a time-series result down to a fixed number of representative rows before QuestDB sends it to the client. A chart can ask for as many points as it can draw instead of fetching millions of rows. Unlike SAMPLE BY, SUBSAMPLE returns original rows, not aggregates, so every column of a selected row is unchanged.

SELECT ... FROM ... [WHERE ...] [SAMPLE BY ...] SUBSAMPLE method(args) [ORDER BY ...] [LIMIT ...]

The methods are lttb, m4, minmax, uniform, cadence and sdt. Input size is capped by cairo.sql.subsample.max.rows (default 100,000,000). subsample is now a reserved word (see Breaking changes). #7013

New SQL capabilities

  • percentile_disc and percentile_cont are now available as aggregates and as whole-partition window functions, with quantile_disc / quantile_cont aliases. They also accept an array of percentiles and return DOUBLE[], e.g. percentile_cont(price, ARRAY[0.5, 0.95, 0.99]). approx_percentile gains the same array form. As part of this change, approx_percentile and approx_median no longer return another group's value for empty groups. #6680
  • HORIZON JOIN supports right-hand filters, either in ON (ON (t.sym = q.sym AND q.venue = 'A')) or as a filtered subquery (HORIZON JOIN (quotes WHERE venue = 'A') q). The filter runs before ASOF matching, so each row matches the latest qualifying right-hand row. Before this change, non-key ON predicates were silently ignored. #7688
  • HORIZON JOIN without aggregates returns one row per left-hand row and offset, and keeps the left-hand designated timestamp. #7682
  • Audited views and IN lists in DECLARE. A DECLARE ... AUDITED @var marks view parameters whose resolved values QuestDB Enterprise records on each read. A declared variable can now hold the list that an IN filter tests against. #7602
  • lag() / lead() work over SYMBOL columns. #7351

Faster queries and ingestion

  • Parallel GROUP BY over hash joins. A GROUP BY (or a SAMPLE BY rewritten to one) over an INNER, LEFT or eligible RIGHT equi-join now builds one shared hash table and joins and aggregates on the worker pool. In the PR's 4M-row Parquet LEFT JOIN benchmark, latency dropped from about 101 ms to 50 ms and peak memory from 308 MB to 165 MB. This is on by default; cairo.sql.parallel.hash.join.groupby.enabled=false turns it off. #7618
  • LATEST ON is faster. Filtered and multi-symbol LATEST ON queries ran 2.9-7.1x faster on the PR's benchmark. A key filter outside a LATEST ON subquery is now pushed inside, so QuestDB finds the latest row only for the requested keys. #7655, #7615
  • LIKE, ILIKE and regex filters on indexed SYMBOL columns can use the index, including the negated forms. Selective patterns ran 35-73x faster in the PR's benchmark. Broad patterns fall back to a scan. cairo.sql.symbol.pattern.index.enabled controls this. #7354
  • Calendar-aligned SAMPLE BY with a DST time zone runs up to about 65% faster for day buckets. #7706
  • Out-of-order commits on XFS no longer wait on a synchronous disk write per column. In the PR's test, posix_fallocate time during WAL apply fell from 2,171 ms to 28 ms. #7795
  • Fewer ingestion and query stalls from slow munmap, which no longer runs while holding a process-wide lock. #7771
  • Joins on SYMBOL keys use less memory. Their symbol translation caches moved off-heap and count toward the per-query memory limit. Some join shapes run slower: LT and two-key ASOF JOINs ran 1.16-1.22x slower, and HORIZON JOINs 1.46-1.51x slower, at the default cairo.sql.join.symbol.translation.cache.capacity. #7650
  • CREATE TABLE with many SYMBOL columns is faster in nosync commit mode. #7912
  • Worker fibers reduce GC pressure and resume latency for suspendable SQL and protocol work. #7379, #7561

Storage and operations

  • Merge-append partitions (opt-in). With cairo.o3.partition.merge.append.enabled, a backdated write into a cold partition appends the touched rows instead of rewriting the whole partition. This cuts O3 write amplification. The partition keeps superseded data as dead space until compaction reclaims it. The flag is off by default. Every non-read-only server now runs a partition-compaction worker, controlled by cairo.partition.compaction.check.interval (default 2 minutes; a negative value disables it). #7595
  • Global metrics are persisted to sys.metrics, a day-partitioned table with configurable sampling, TTL and exclusions. metrics.persist.enabled is on by default. #7634
  • Retryable bounded shutdown. Embedders and deployment controllers can stop the server within a deadline, then retry. #7540

QWP, security and Web Console

  • Browsers can connect to QWP over WebSocket, either same-origin with session-cookie authentication or cross-origin through the reloadable qwp.browser.allowed.origins allowlist. Capability negotiation also works without custom headers. #7531, #7683
  • Large QWP query results no longer crash the server. In a 50-million-row read, peak RSS fell from 6.40 GiB to 462 MiB. Rows left over from a cancelled query no longer reach the next query on the same connection. #7755
  • ILP-over-HTTP authorizes each request as its own identity. Before this fix, a keep-alive connection could check later commits against the identity of the first writer. #7643
  • Web Console 2.0.5 adds live views support, a query activity drawer, an option to run the full query text, and rule-based trends in the result grid. #7691

Correctness fixes

This release fixes wrong results, compile failures, hangs and crashes across HORIZON JOIN, WINDOW JOIN, SAMPLE BY (including FILL), ORDER BY, LATEST ON and dateadd() queries. It also fixes filters over UUID, IPv4, CHAR, SYMBOL and BOOLEAN columns, covering and posting indexes, parallel filtered scans, and materialized view refresh. Other fixes cover log writer hangs and failures, Parquet rewrites after a column type change, and resumed HTTP static file downloads. #7681, #7550, #7871, #7877, #7664, #7675, #7880
